item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russia is stepping up airstrikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, killing civilians in Zaporizhzhia and hitting power plants in Kyiv, while Ukraine says it will pause its own refinery strikes if Russia ends the energy attacks. Ukraine struck a Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile maintenance base and accused SpaceX of throttling Starlink terminals used by Kyiv forces for drones. Russian authorities detained a Japanese journalist on espionage charges and announced a diesel deal framed as an energy ceasefire, which Ukraine called false after further strikes. The UCDP recorded 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli forces have blocked construction of a Gaza base created by the Trump peace board and continued air strikes that killed a Palestinian woman in Gaza City while rescuing a girl from a burning apartment. Israel has detained over 2,000 Palestinian children since 2023 and is pursuing defamation lawsuits against former security chiefs for statements about the October 7 attacks. Iran has seen two container ships sink near the Strait of Hormuz amid a surge in Iranian attacks, linking regional tensions to the Gaza conflict. A judge has blocked US sanctions on rights groups assisting the ICC Gaza war crimes inquiry. The conflict caused 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:

Clashes in Amhara have left at least 183 people dead, according to the UN, and the United Nations has allocated $8.5 million for emergency humanitarian response in northern Ethiopia. Leaders from Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia are meeting to coordinate security operations if the conflict spreads across borders. Washington has called for de-escalation as Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions rise. The conflict has caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:

The federal government is deepening defence ties with Pakistan, seeking JF‑17 fighter jets and securing the release of four Pakistani sailors from Somali pirates. Somali forces killed two al-Shabaab militants in the Bay region and a military court linked a father’s killing to the 2017 Mogadishu bombing case; the lower house passed a long-delayed anti-rape bill and a market shooting in Garowe left two dead and four wounded.
